description: Rocom conformance requirement registry — Part 6 (Security/Identity) and Part 7 (Data Governance)

requirements.statement: Every agent presents a unique X.509 client certificate. Shared certificates rejected.
Manual revocation supported: a revoked agent is denied within one operational day.
Certificate rotation without service interruption.
Revocation propagated to all brokers/endpoints within deployment profile.
Network zone model enforced: OT→IT only via convergence layer.
Fully automatic issuance and rotation (SPIRE or equivalent).
Central revocation authority with signed revocation feed; propagation under 5 minutes.
Onboarding/offboarding triggers identity issuance/revocation atomically.
Compromise response: flagged agent quarantined within 5 minutes.
Every agent has a data profile in the Agent Registry: sensors, data classes, declared destinations, lawful basis.
Every provider/task-source connection declares data_classes_delivered, declared_destinations, lawful_basis.
Sensor-payload class does not traverse the convergence layer.
Operational telemetry is verified free of personal-data fields.
All vendor telemetry/diagnostic egress is declared, routable and blockable.
Data flows are attributable to agent identity in the audit trail.
Registry can export an Article 30-compatible record of processing.
Egress policy enforced technically at convergence layer (allow-list per agent identity). Policy changes versioned and approved (two-person rule).
Continuous verification: declared data profiles reconciled against observed flows; deviations raise governance events within 24h.
Third-country transfer register auditable per art. 30 with per-transfer lawful-basis reference.
Teleoperation/remote assistance MAY carry sensor payloads as declared exception.
